sources.label: Repo spec — rq-artifactPathTruth01 + rq-isolSessionTaskQueue04
sources.summary: Both fixes are already spec-mandated: artifact reads must consult projection and source-tag/omit phantom paths; diagnostics must emit per-queue rows with type label + owning session. Design implements existing law.

subagent_reports.architecture_assessment: Both fixes are sound and reuse tested infrastructure. Fix 1 adds a tier to an existing fallback chain; the projection (change.json state.documents) is written per-signal by the writeChangeProjection activity (workflows.ts:999-1025), so it is a durable mirror of committed workflow state — strictly more correct than the legacy markdown tier, which is archive-only (CHANGELOG.md:35; no active write path found via lgrep). Fix 2 ports the session-queue probe already proven in status-health.ts:431-466 into doctor, which today passes a bare projectId (doctor.ts:268) and probes only the project queue. Temporal semantics fully support both decisions: a no-poller Query fails fast with FAILED_PRECONDITION/DEADLINE_EXCEEDED (not SDK-auto-retried; Query tasks are sync-matched and never persisted), so not retrying is correct; reading from an external committed projection when the Query is unavailable is the idiomatic cache-aside pattern (workflow history stays authoritative). Two caution-level refinements: (R1) prefer projection BEFORE markdown in the fallback order to avoid a narrow staleness window for pre-migration leftover markdown; (R2) propagate an explicit source/degradation marker so callers cannot infer workflow liveness from a successful projection read. Neither blocks the defect fix. The doctor session-probe must classify per-queue state (fresh/stale/none/unavailable) plus owning-session rather than collapsing to binary healthy.

validation.notes: No blockers. Design fixes the defect and aligns with Temporal docs + repo spec (rq-artifactPathTruth01, rq-isolSessionTaskQueue04). Two caution-level refinements: (R1) projection-before-markdown ordering — narrow correctness window for pre-migration stale markdown; (R2) explicit source/degradation marker. Apply Fix 1 to BOTH readArtifact (artifacts.ts:89) and readArtifacts batch path (artifacts.ts:177). Doctor session-probe must classify (not binary-collapse) and treat a dead owning-session's absent poller as informational, not red.

tradeoffs: Projection-as-fallback serves content at most one committed-signal behind live workflow state; harmless for finalized narrative artifacts but technically stale vs a successful live Query — acceptable because Query is tried first and is authoritative.

Adding DescribeTaskQueue calls for session queues consumes visibility/frontend RPS budget (server >=1.24 binds DTQ to visibility limits); mitigated by the existing 30s pollerProbeCache and Temporal's own server-side DTQ caching (PR #6572/#6643).
Markdown-before-projection ordering is safe for active/archived changes but risks serving stale pre-migration leftover markdown; projection-first eliminates that window.
Source/degradation marker adds a field to the read result type but enables the no-silent-success observability theme and prevents liveness-inference from a fallback read.

alternatives_considered.option: Consult projection FIRST, Query second (disk-first hydration flip)
alternatives_considered.rationale: Explicitly ruled out in OUT_OF_SCOPE. For a live workflow the Query is strictly more current than any disk snapshot; Query-first is correct and the projection is only the fallback. Flipping would serve marginally-staler content on the hot path.

alternatives_considered.option: Retry the timed-out Query before falling back
alternatives_considered.rationale: Temporal confirms no-poller Query fails with FAILED_PRECONDITION/DEADLINE_EXCEEDED, which the TS SDK does NOT auto-retry (grpc-retry.ts retryable set excludes both codes); Query tasks are sync-matched and never persisted, so retry re-burns the 8s aggregate read budget against an unchanging condition. The design's fatal-classification of TemporalQueryTimeoutError is correct.

Fixes the defect and is safe for active (markdown absent) and archived (consistent) changes, but projection is the authoritative mirror of workflow state and markdown is archive-only; projection-first is cleaner and closes a narrow pre-migration-stale-markdown window. Defer the proposed order in favor of projection-first.

alternatives_considered.option: Binary healthy/unhealthy session-queue verdict in doctor
alternatives_considered.rationale: DescribeTaskQueue poller-absence has documented false-positive vectors (worker at capacity stops polling; 2-min sliding window). Must report fresh/stale/none/unavailable + owning-session (per rq-isolSessionTaskQueue04) and treat a dead session's absent poller as informational, else the fix trades false-green for false-red.

architecture_judgement.recommendation: Proceed to implement with two folded-in refinements: (R1) order the new projection tier BEFORE the legacy markdown tier (Query -> projection -> markdown -> archive); (R2) return/source-tag the read with its provenance (workflow | active_projection | retired_projection | disk | archive) so callers can distinguish authoritative-live from fallback. Apply the tier to both readArtifact and the batched readArtifacts. For Fix 2, mirror status-health.ts:431-466 into doctor, emit per-queue rows with type label + owning-session, degrade cleanly when no sessionId, and classify session-queue poller-absence as informational when the owning session is dead vs red only when the session is expected-alive.

subagent_reports.recommendation: READY with caution. Land both fixes; fold in R1 (projection-before-markdown) and R2 (source marker) since they are cheap and improve correctness/observability. Apply Fix 1 to both readArtifact and readArtifacts. Confirm Temporal dev/local frontend.namespaceRPS.visibility headroom is adequate for the added per-session DTQ call (30s cache bounds steady-state to ~1 DTQ/queue/30s).
follow_ups: If markdown-before-projection is retained, add a regression test: active change with a stale legacy proposal.md AND a fresher projection document -> assert projection content wins.
Verify the 8s aggregate read budget referenced in the prompt is documented/enforced where the Query is attempted, so the no-retry decision's budget claim is structural rather than prose-only (P38).
Consider surfacing the read source field through adv_change_show include flags so consumers can observe when reads are degrading to projection (observability for the no-silent-success theme).

changes.body: ADV read surfaces MUST NOT expose nonexistent active artifact filesystem paths as readable source-of-truth. When artifact content lives in Temporal state.documents, tools MUST expose content via ADV read/include fields and either omit filesystem paths or mark them machine-readably non-readable/source-tagged. Artifact readback MUST consult the durable disk projection's `documents` map before concluding content is absent, using the precedence Temporal workflow Query, then projection `documents`, then legacy disk artifact, then archive bundle; the projection tier MUST NOT be consulted before the workflow Query. Every resolved artifact read MUST carry a machine-readable source tag identifying which tier served it, so a caller cannot infer workflow queryability from the presence of content. A local projection read MUST remain reachable even when the request-scoped Temporal aggregate read deadline is already exhausted. Legacy disk and archive-bundle fallback reads MUST remain supported.

## Intent

Close two coupled defects that make ADV narrative artifact content unreadable, and make the health surface capable of reporting the condition.

1. `readArtifact` never falls back to the disk projection's `documents` field. When a change's originating session is gone, its workflow sits on an unpolled session task queue, the Temporal Query is never served, and artifact content becomes unreachable — even though the content is intact in `change.json`.
2. `adv_doctor` probes only the project task queue, so it reports `queue_serviceable: true` during exactly the session-queue orphaning that causes defect 1.

## Root Cause Analysis

### Observed symptom

Reading narrative artifacts for change `fixTaskUpdatePersistence` failed repeatedly:

```
adv_change_show include:{executiveSummary:true, artifactOnly:true}
→ _artifactsError: "Temporal operation exceeded 1500ms timeout"
→ hydrationStats: { deadlineExceeded: true, omitted: ["artifacts"] }
```

Reproduced across ~40 minutes and multiple load conditions. Metadata reads succeeded instantly throughout. The artifact existed and was hash-verified (`b7c454dd…`, 1084 non-whitespace chars, `updatedAt` 2026-08-01T22:21:50Z).

### Causal chain

1. Change workflows run on **session-scoped** task queues, `advance-{projectId}-{sessionId}` (`plugin/src/temporal/client.ts:55-60`), selected at `plugin/src/temporal/operations.ts:1030-1033`.
2. `fixTaskUpdatePersistence` was created 2026-08-01 by a session that no longer exists. Its workflow remains RUNNING on that dead session's queue. Adoption only adds pollers and never re-routes workflows (spec `advance-workflow.md:6678`), and Temporal task queues have no reclamation.
3. Artifact content is read via a live Temporal workflow Query — `changeStateQuery` (`plugin/src/temporal/messages.ts:118-122`), issued at `plugin/src/storage/store-temporal/index.ts:765-768`. Temporal documents this as requiring a live worker: *"A Worker must be online to process the query"*; with no poller the server returns `FAILED_PRECONDITION` / `DEADLINE_EXCEEDED`.
4. `TemporalQueryTimeoutError` is deliberately classified `fatal` (`plugin/src/temporal/retry-wrapper.ts:149`), so it is not retried — correct behavior, but it makes the failure terminal for the request.
5. `readArtifact` (`plugin/src/tools/change/artifacts.ts:89-125`) does have fallbacks, but they are: legacy markdown file (`<changesDir>/<changeId>/proposal.md`), then archive bundle. **Neither consults `change.json` → `documents`.** For an active change that never had legacy markdown written, the fallback yields empty.

### The decisive finding

The disk projection **already carries artifact content**:

- `mapTemporalChangeStateToChange` returns `documents: safeState.documents` (`plugin/src/storage/store-temporal/shared.ts:111`)
- `TEMPORAL_OWNED_PROJECTION_FIELDS` includes `documents` and `artifacts` (`shared.ts:143-176`)
- `projectTemporalStateOntoLatest` merges them (`shared.ts:183-193`)
- `commitChangeProjection` writes the full value atomically to `change.json` (`plugin/src/storage/change-projection-transaction.ts:367-376`)
- `context-snapshot-fetch.ts:27` already reads `change.documents?.proposal` successfully

Confirmed empirically: `adv_change_show` returned `documents: "[truncated: 17617 chars]"` with `_source: "disk"` while the artifact hydration path simultaneously failed. The content was on disk and being returned by the store the whole time; only the artifact read path failed to look there.

**Root cause: the artifact read path has a missing fallback tier, not a data-loss or contention problem.** Contention only explains the fluctuating deadline values (1500ms vs 702ms), which are the per-attempt cap (`retry-wrapper.ts:329-332`) clipped by the 8s aggregate budget (`retry-wrapper.ts:203`) after `loadDiskProjection` consumed ~7.3s. Those are local timer expirations on an unrouted query, not worker saturation — genuine contention would push waits above the cap, not below it.

### Why this was not caught

`adv_doctor` reported `healthy` with `queue_serviceable: true` throughout. Its probe targets only `buildProjectTaskQueue(projectId)` (`plugin/src/tools/doctor.ts:190-205`, called at `:324` and `:731`). Every session co-polls the project queue (`plugin/src/plugin-init.ts:273`), so the probe is green whenever the *current* session's worker is alive. It is structurally incapable of detecting an orphaned session queue.

The multi-target probe capability already exists — `probeQueues(targets: QueueProbeTarget[])` with `queueType: "session" | "project"` (`plugin/src/temporal/health-probe.ts:107-158`) — and `status-health.ts:424-466` already uses it correctly. Only the doctor call site fails to pass session targets.

### Contributing design context (not in scope to change here)

Storing document content in workflow state and reading it back solely via Query is a documented Temporal anti-pattern (external-storage offload threshold is 256 KiB; ADV documents run ~200KB). The architectural resolution is tracked as `bl-MsU7dzK0` (ephemeral workflow + disk-durable record). Consolidating task queues is explicitly **not** the fix: `rq-isolSessionTaskQueue01` is priority `must` and exists so a peer session's wedged worker cannot block another session, and Temporal provides no API to change a running workflow's TaskQueue — ~52 in-flight changes would strand.

## LBP Targets

- Fallback ordering for artifact reads: Temporal Query → legacy markdown → `change.json.documents` → archive bundle
- `rq-artifactPathTruth01` explicitly requires "legacy disk and archive-bundle fallback reads MUST remain supported" — confirm an added tier is consistent
- Confirm Fix 3 closes rather than violates `rq-isolSessionTaskQueue04` (which already mandates per-queue serviceability with type labels)
- Confirm no violation of the `no-disk-writes-invariant` structural law (it governs the write API, not projection shape)

## Scope

- `plugin/src/tools/change/artifacts.ts` — add disk-projection `documents` fallback tier to `readArtifact` and `readArtifacts`
- `plugin/src/tools/doctor.ts` — probe session task queues alongside the project queue
- Tests for both paths

Out of scope: task-queue topology changes; the full `bl-HiZJbUuy` Query-first → disk-first hydration flip; `bl-MsU7dzK0` workflow lifecycle rework.

## User Outcomes

- Artifact reads keep working when a change's originating session is gone — no OpenCode restart, no waiting for contention
- `adv_doctor` reports unhealthy when a session queue is unpolled, instead of a false green
- The stalled `fixTaskUpdatePersistence` release unblocks

## Existing Scope Involved

- `bl-HiZJbUuy` (disk-authoritative active-change reads) — this is its first narrow slice; the item stays open for the broader hydration flip
- `bl-workerQueueReadBlackout` — Fix 3 supplies its missing diagnostics; its claim that the orphan adopter is never constructed in non-lock-owning hosts is **refuted** under default config (`worker_singleton_enforce` defaults false; `plugin-init.ts:721-727` constructs unconditionally)
- `rq-isolSessionTaskQueue04` — currently violated by the doctor; this change closes the gap

## Spec-Law Impact Assessment

**Outcome: Modify** (one requirement), plus one pure-conformance fix requiring no law change.

### Fix 1 — artifact read fallback → MODIFY `rq-artifactPathTruth01`

Current body enumerates supported fallback sources as *"Legacy disk and archive-bundle fallback reads MUST remain supported."* Scenario `rq-artifactPathTruth01.2` covers exactly those two tiers. The disk-projection `documents` tier is **not** covered by existing law, yet it is the tier that makes content readable when a workflow's session queue is orphaned.

**Draft spec-delta obligation:**

- **Capability:** `advance-workflow`
- **Delta kind:** `modify`
- **Requirement:** `rq-artifactPathTruth01` ("Truthful Artifact Path Read Surfaces")
- **Change:** Require artifact readback to consult the durable disk projection's `documents` map before concluding content is absent, and to source-tag returned content with its provenance. Ordering: Temporal Query → projection `documents` → legacy disk artifact → archive bundle.
- **New scenario `rq-artifactPathTruth01.4` — Projection documents serve artifact reads when the workflow is unreachable:**
  - **Given** an active change whose `state.documents.executiveSummary` was persisted to the disk projection
  - **And** the change's workflow is RUNNING on a task queue with no live poller (originating session ended)
  - **When** artifact readback runs for that change
  - **Then** the executive-summary content is returned from the projection `documents` map
  - **And** the response does not report the artifact as unreadable or absent
  - **And** no filesystem path is exposed for the projection-sourced content
- **New scenario `rq-artifactPathTruth01.5` — Artifact reads declare provenance:**
  - **Given** artifact content is returned from any tier
  - **When** the read surface emits the result
  - **Then** the result carries a machine-readable source tag distinguishing authoritative live workflow reads from projection, legacy-disk, and archive-bundle fallbacks
  - **And** a caller cannot infer workflow queryability from the mere presence of content
- **Rationale:** The projection already persists `documents` (`shared.ts:111`, `TEMPORAL_OWNED_PROJECTION_FIELDS` at `shared.ts:143-176`, written by the `writeChangeProjection` activity, `workflows.ts:999-1025`, committed by `change-projection-transaction.ts:367-376`). Law currently permits a read surface to report content unreachable while that content sits durably on disk.

**Compatibility with existing law:**
- `rq-artifactPathTruth01.2` — preserved; this adds a tier and reorders, removes none.
- `rq-artifactPathTruth01.1` (no fake readable path) — preserved and strengthened by the provenance tag.
- `rq-artifactPathTruth01.3` — untouched.
- `no-disk-writes-invariant` (`plugin/src/storage/store-temporal/no-disk-writes-invariant.test.ts`) — **not violated**. It governs the *write* API (content flows through signals, not `create`/`updateArtifacts` disk writes). This change is read-only.

### Fix 3 — doctor session-queue probing → NO SPEC LAW UPDATE REQUIRED

`rq-isolSessionTaskQueue04` (priority `must`) already mandates the behavior verbatim, including per-queue type labels and owning-session identification (`04.1`). `adv_doctor` currently probes only `buildProjectTaskQueue(projectId)` (`doctor.ts:190-205`, called at `:324` and `:731`) — a live violation of shipped law. This is conformance work. Scenario `04.3` (legacy single-queue API back-compat) must remain green.

## Validated Design (adv-researcher: READY with caution — both refinements adopted)

### R1 — Precedence: Query → projection → markdown → archive

Query-first is correct: the live workflow is strictly most current. Projection is a durable mirror written per-signal by the `writeChangeProjection` activity (`workflows.ts:999-1025`).

**Refinement adopted:** projection is consulted **before** legacy markdown, not after. Legacy markdown is archive-era only — there are no active write paths to it — so for active changes that tier is always empty, and markdown-first risks serving stale pre-migration leftovers over the authoritative mirror.

**Staleness bound:** one signal's projection-activity round-trip. A stale read is possible only mid-edit, which the gate model excludes for finalized narrative artifacts. Projection MUST NOT be consulted before the Query.

### R2 — Provenance tagging (no silent degradation)

Returning fallback content without a marker would let a caller infer "content returned ⇒ workflow queryable," which is false. Given this codebase's active theme of eliminating silent success, every artifact read carries a machine-readable source tag. The taxonomy already exists — `LoadResult.source` (`change-projection-reader.ts:192-198`): `workflow | disk | archive | active_projection | retired_projection | read_model`.

### Fix 3 classification — avoid trading false-green for false-red

Pollers legitimately vanish from `DescribeTaskQueue` after ~1-2 minutes idle, or when a worker is at capacity. Absence is necessary but not sufficient evidence of a problem.

- Report a graded status — `fresh | stale | none | unavailable` — never a binary healthy/unhealthy collapse.
- Include the owning session per `rq-isolSessionTaskQueue04.1`.
- An absent poller on a **dead session's** queue is *informational*; escalate to red only when the owning session is expected-alive.
- Reuse the proven classification at `status-health.ts:431-466`.

### Temporal guidance confirmed

- Not retrying the timed-out Query is correct. No-poller Query returns `FAILED_PRECONDITION` (code 9) — [TS message-passing](https://docs.temporal.io/develop/typescript/workflows/message-passing); the SDK grpc-retry set excludes both `FAILED_PRECONDITION` and `DEADLINE_EXCEEDED`. Query Tasks are not persisted and are sync-matched only when polled ([task-queue docs](https://docs.temporal.io/task-queue)), so retry is futile until a poller returns.
- Reading workflow-associated application data from an external projection is idiomatic cache-aside; workflow history remains authoritative.
- `DescribeTaskQueue` is the canonical health mechanism but is bound to the visibility RPS limiter on server ≥1.24. The existing 30s poller cache (`health-probe.ts:101-105`) is adequate and matches Temporal's own caching guidance.

## Implementation Strategy

### Fix 3 — doctor session-queue probing

- Generalize `probeQueue` (`doctor.ts:190-205`) to accept a queue name + type rather than hardcoding `buildProjectTaskQueue`.
- At the serviceability call sites (`:319-326`, `:730-731`), probe both the project queue and the current session queue via `getCurrentSessionId()` (`utils/session-id.ts:42-58`).
- Emit per-queue rows with `queueType` and owning session; classify graded, not binary.
- Degrade cleanly when no session id is available — skip the session probe, preserve existing output shape (`04.3`).

### Fix 1 — artifact read fallback tier

- Insert the projection tier into `readArtifact` (`artifacts.ts:89-125`) immediately after the Temporal Query, before legacy markdown: load via `loadChange` (`change-projection-reader.ts:368`), read `documents[kind]`.
- Apply the identical tier to the batched `readArtifacts` (`artifacts.ts:177-225`) — same gap, parallel code path.
- Source-tag every result; expose no filesystem path for projection-sourced content. `normalizeArtifactMetadataForReadback` (`:32-58`) already marks `source === "temporal"` as `readable: false`; projection-sourced content must be equally honest.
- Add no retry against the failed Query.
- Do not alter write paths.

### Explicitly out of scope

- Task-queue topology changes. `rq-isolSessionTaskQueue01` is priority `must`; Temporal offers no API to change a running workflow's TaskQueue, so ~52 in-flight changes would strand.
- The full `bl-HiZJbUuy` Query-first → disk-first hydration flip for `adv_change_show`/`list`/`gate_status`/`wip_state`.
- `bl-MsU7dzK0` ephemeral-workflow lifecycle rework.

# Executive Summary — Fix artifact read fallback

## Outcome

ADV can now read a change's written record even when the background process that normally serves it has gone away, and its health check now tells you when that has happened instead of reporting all-clear.

## Why it matters

Work in ADV is tracked by a long-running background process, one per working session. When a session ends, its process can be left stranded: still holding real, completed work, but with nobody left listening to answer questions about it. Before this change, that produced a silent, misleading failure.

- **The record looked lost.** Asking ADV for a change's proposal, design, or agreement returned nothing — as though the work had never been done. The content was never actually lost; a durable copy was always on disk. ADV simply never looked there.
- **The health check said everything was fine.** Running the diagnostic reported "System healthy; no action needed" while reads were actively failing, sending anyone investigating in the wrong direction.

This change was validated against itself. While the work was being finished, this very change hit the exact fault it fixes: its own task list became unreadable, and the diagnostic reported full health. Diagnosing that took a dedicated investigation session — precisely the wasted effort this change eliminates.

## What was delivered

- **Reads fall back to the durable copy.** When the live source cannot answer, ADV now reads the durable on-disk copy instead of reporting the content missing. The fallback works even when the time budget for the live attempt is already spent, which is the common case in this fault.
- **Every read says where it came from.** Results are tagged with their source, so content served from a fallback can never be mistaken for a confirmed-live read. This preserves the ability to detect the underlying fault rather than hiding it.
- **No wasted retries.** A live source that has already failed for this reason is not asked again; the fallback is used directly.
- **The diagnostic now surfaces the real condition.** It reports the serving status of both the session and the project queue, graded as fresh, stale, none, or unavailable rather than a single pass/fail flag.
- **Stranded work is flagged without noise.** A quiet queue from an ended session is normal and is deliberately not reported on its own. It is reported only when it still holds unfinished work — the genuinely abnormal case, and the one behind the original outage. This is capped at a bounded number of checks so the diagnostic stays cheap.

## Verification

- Full test suite: 541 files, 8298 tests, 0 failures.
- Static checks, type checks, schema, manifest, and formatting checks: all clean, 0 errors.
- A test reproducing the original production fault fails before the fix and passes after it.
- Two independent review passes. The first blocked the change on a real gap: the diagnostic did not cover queues from ended sessions, so the original outage would still have gone undetected. That gap was closed and re-reviewed.
- A second gap found during re-review — status rows appearing only after a repair ran, not on a normal diagnostic run — was also corrected.

## Risks and follow-ups

- **Deployment required before any benefit is visible.** These are read and diagnostic paths in the plugin. Nothing changes for a running system until the change is merged to the default branch, rebuilt, deployed, and the host restarted.
- **Diagnostic coverage is intentionally bounded.** It checks the oldest few stranded queues, not all of them, to keep the check cheap. If more are stranded than the cap, the diagnostic says so rather than silently truncating.
- **One flaky test, unrelated to this work.** A gate test is sensitive to ordering when the full suite runs in parallel. It passes in isolation and on rerun, and does not involve this change's code. Logged as a low-priority follow-up.
- **No change to how work is written or stored.** This change only affects reading and diagnostics, so it carries no data migration and no impact on recorded history.
